subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / follow-up: Acme Health
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / follow-up: Acme Health

Thanks Liam — great conversation today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a dedicated proposal: 

Recap from today's discovery:
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + structured extraction for patient intake flows.
- Typical output length: ~250-1,000 tokens per response depending on template.
- Current expectation: ~450M tokens/month on average, with occasional bursts.

Open items we need to confirm to produce a firm dedicated capacity quote:
1) Confirm monthly and peak token volumes (daily and burst windows).
2) Target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range you have in mind for dedicated capacity commitment.
3) Throughput & latency SLAs: target E2E latency, concurrent live requests, and burst length.
4) GPU preference: A100 (80GB) vs H100, and whether you need NVMe-backed KV cache for large context.
5) Commitment term (monthly, 3/6/12 months) — longer terms unlock better unit economics.

To make things concrete, can you confirm the numbers from our call or correct them if I misunderstood? Based on what we discussed, I can run three options (4x A100 reserved, 8x A100 reserved, 4x H100 reserved) and show expected throughput and indicative $/1M tokens.

Next steps: if you can reply with the confirmation on volumes, budget target ($/1M tokens), and preferred GPU family, I’ll get you an initial proposal and a draft SLA/contract for procurement to review.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_q2_traffic.xlsx (traffic estimates), SLA-draft.pdf (sample dedicated SLA)

From: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / follow-up: Acme Health

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Below are the numbers from our side: 

- Typical monthly volume: ~450M tokens (this is our expectation for steady-state once we onboard new clinics).
- Peak/day: up to ~25M tokens on big intake days (we see concentrated traffic during morning batch windows).
- Burst profile: short bursts up to ~6,000 tokens/sec for ~5-10 minutes (during large onboarding waves).
- Concurrent live requests: ~30-50 (many small requests ~200-1,000 tokens each).
- Latency target: prefer <= 600ms P95 for interactive flows, tolerable up to 1s for batch jobs.

Budget and unit-econ goal:
- Monthly budget range for dedicated capacity: $20k- $30k/month to start (we have room to expand).
- Target unit economics: ideally around $55 / 1M tokens (open to tradeoffs for better latency / reserved capacity).

GPU preference: we don’t have a hard preference, but the team is leaning toward A100 (80GB) unless you recommend H100 for noticeable perf gains on our model variants.

Happy to run the 3-month pilot if that helps get to a firm number. Let me know what you need from procurement to move forward.

—
Liam O'Reilly
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / follow-up: Acme Health

Great — that gives us everything we need to put together an initial sided proposal. A few quick notes and an indicative pricing exercise based on your numbers (450M tokens/month, peak bursts up to 6k tokens/sec):

Indicative reserved configs (monthly, list price estimates):
- Option A: 4 x A100 (80GB), reserved capacity with autoscaling to 6x for bursts — list est: $30,000/month. Indicative $/1M tokens at 450M tokens = ~$66.7 / 1M tokens.
- Option B: 8 x A100 (80GB), reserved — list est: $55,000/month. Indicative $/1M tokens = ~$122 / 1M tokens (higher but higher headroom for concurrency).
- Option C: 4 x H100 (80GB), reserved — list est: $50,000/month. Indicative $/1M tokens = ~$111 / 1M tokens (higher HW cost, lower latency for some models).

Notes and levers to hit your $55 / 1M target:
- At list-priced reserved capacity, Option A is closest to your target but still ~20% above $55. We can improve unit economics via: longer-term commitment (6-12 months), higher utilization through batching & KV/prefix caching (we can typically recover 10-30% token costs for summary/extraction workloads), and small model quantization where acceptable.
- For your burst profile, 4xA100 with autoscale to 6x should handle 6k tokens/sec bursts of 5-10 minutes with P95 latency in your target range, assuming a 1-2 GPU serving sharding strategy and Redwood's dynamic batching.

Recommended next steps:
1) We’ll draft a 3-month pilot SOW on 4x A100 reserved with autoscale to 6x and target monthly cap of 450M tokens — this will show real utilization and let us refine $/1M.
2) If procurement wants improved unit economics up front, we can present a 12-month commitment price that brings indicative $/1M closer to $50-55.
3) I’ll attach a short technical appendix on throughput assumptions (model configs, batch sizes, KV caching expectations) for your infra team to validate.

If that sounds good, I’ll circulate a formal pilot proposal + draft contract and ask Monica (CS lead) to define onboarding milestones. Will you or procurement be the signer for a pilot SOW?

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: technical-appendix.pdf (includes throughput assumptions)

From: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / follow-up: Acme Health

Thanks Marcus — that all looks reasonable. We’re happy to pilot the 4x A100 reserved with autoscale to 6x for a 3-month SOW. Procurement will handle the SOW signature.

Next steps for us:
- Procurement to review draft SOW and SLA (please send DocuSign).
- We’ll share any additional traffic slices from acme_q2_traffic.xlsx that show worst-case days so you can validate burst handling.
- Target: start pilot the week of Mar 16, pending procurement review.

Can you put together the pilot SOW and include the commitment vs. month-to-month economics so we can see the delta to hit the $55 / 1M target? If possible, include a simple utilization sensitivity table (450M vs 600M tokens/month).

Appreciate the quick turn.

—
Liam O'Reilly
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
liam.oreilly@acmehealth.com

Attachments: none
